audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers said opposite things. The full layer gave Galio all seven rows and rated the lane HARD 8/10 with a 'anti-LeBlanc statue' framing, while the content layer gave LeBlanc all seven rows and called it 'one of the softest lane matchups you'll find'. Every phases[N].why described LeBlanc winning under a row labelled Galio.
audit.why: 51.62% over 2586 games, and the packet levelChart, both land between those two extremes but on LeBlanc's side. Galio's threat is a 275-range taunt and a 11s knockup dash — real, but not a 8/10 lane; his own kill pressure into a ranged burst mage is low.
audit.corrected: phases[0..6].side -> LeBlanc (matching win[], which already read LeBlanc), ratings pulled to 6/10 and 5/10, and the lane re-rated EVEN 6/10 with breakdown.difficulty and report[14] updated to agree.

audit.whatIsWrong: Content repeatedly said Galio has 'no dash before 6' / 'no gap-close before 6'.
audit.why: Justice Punch is a basic ability — 11/10/9/8/7 — that steps back, charges, and knocks up the first champion hit. It is available from level 3 and is his entire engage. His level 6 (Hero's Entrance, 180/160/140) genuinely is a roam tool that lands on an ally, so the spike that matters in lane is the E, not the R.
audit.corrected: Justice Punch named as an 11s knockup dash from level 3 in early, spikes[0], whys[2] and the cooldowns field; Hero's Entrance given its 180s cost so you can track when he leaves.

audit.whatIsWrong: The shield was called his 'passive shield'; Colossal Smash's auto-attack reset was never mentioned.
audit.why: Colossal Smash is the passive — every few seconds his next basic attack deals bonus damage in an area, which is an auto reset and the tell before he commits. The shield sits on Shield of Durand (W, 18/17/16/15/14), which taunts only inside 275 range, and the other shield is on Hero's Entrance.
audit.corrected: Shield attributed to Shield of Durand with its 275 range; Colossal Smash's reset stated as the step-back cue.

audit.why: Justice Punch 11s->7s, Shield of Durand 18s->14s and Hero's Entrance 180s->140s are what the 'step up only on its downtime' advice was missing.

audit.corrected: Replaced with bodies grounded in Justice Punch's wind-up, Galio's MR/health, and Colossal Smash.

edits.before: Galio is one of the softest lane matchups you'll find — no gap-close before 6, a slow skillshot Q, and a passive shield that only blocks one instance of burst rather than your whole combo. Chunk him every time he farms and all-in the moment his Q or W taunt is down; he simply cannot threaten you back in any 1v1 scenario pre-6.
edits.after: Galio is softer in lane than his reputation — Justice Punch is a knockup dash on 11s from level 3, Winds of War is another 11s, and Shield of Durand only taunts inside 275 range. Chunk him every time he farms and commit the moment his E or the taunt is spent; his own damage cannot take a bar before your return timer expires.

edits.before: His ultimate is a team utility tool (global roam/shield for an ally), not a lane threat, so it changes nothing about your ability to burst him down at 6 — R-E-Q-W still one-shots him if he's ever caught pushed up. Keep shoving him in and roam freely since he has no wave-clear speed or dash to punish you leaving lane. This matchup should be a near-total lockout if you play forward.
edits.after: Hero's Entrance is a team tool — a shield and a landing on an ally, 180s at rank 1 — so his 6 changes nothing in lane, and your full string still chunks him hard whenever he is caught pushed up. Keep shoving and roam freely; he has no wave clear fast enough to punish you leaving. Track that 180s and leave when it does, or you arrive into a collapse he set up.
